rules.title: Source-of-income discrimination ban in housing (including Section 8 and VASH vouchers)
rules.requirement: A California landlord may not refuse to rent to you, or otherwise discriminate against you, because of your lawful, verifiable source of income. This includes public assistance and housing subsidies such as Section 8 and HUD-VASH vouchers. A landlord may still ask about the level or source of your income.
rules.key_value: Source of income, including Section 8 and VASH vouchers, is a protected class
rules.coverage_conditions: Owners of any housing accommodation in California. 'Source of income' means lawful, verifiable income paid to the tenant, to the tenant's representative, or to the landlord on the tenant's behalf. It includes public assistance, housing subsidies, Section 8 vouchers and VASH vouchers.
rules.exemptions: Asking about the level or source of income is not discrimination.
rules.quoted_span: (a) For the owner of any housing accommodation to discriminate against or harass any person because of the race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran or military status, or genetic information of that person.

rules.title: Government rent subsidy holders: income standard on tenant share and alternative to credit history
rules.requirement: If you have a government rent subsidy, a landlord must base any income test on only your share of the rent. A landlord who uses your credit history must let you offer other proof that you can pay your share instead, such as benefit payments, pay records or bank statements. The landlord must give you reasonable time to provide that proof and must reasonably consider it.
rules.key_value: Income test based on tenant's share of rent; alternative evidence must be allowed in place of credit history
rules.coverage_conditions: Rentals in California where the applicant has a government rent subsidy.
rules.exemptions: Landlords may still verify employment, ask for landlord references and verify identity.
rules.quoted_span: (B) (i) Use a person’s credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant’s discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay

notes: Effective dates: the document says only that the section was last amended by SB 267 (Stats. 2023, Ch. 776), effective January 1, 2024. I used that date for subdivision (o), the credit-history rule that SB 267 added. The source-of-income rule's original effective date is not in this document, so I left it null. It was earlier law, believed to be SB 329, effective 2020-01-01; a reviewer should confirm. Subdivision (n) bars income standards that do not count the combined income of unmarried co-applicants the same way as married ones. It relates to tenant screening, but it is really a marital-status rule, so I did not extract it as a separate record. A reviewer may want to add it under screening_restrictions. The other subdivisions (lending, advertising, appraisals, land use, retaliation) are outside the six categories. Exemptions from FEHA, such as an owner-occupied home renting out one room under Gov. Code § 12927, are not in this document, so I did not record them.
